page.overview:
What is S'tya-Yg'Nalle?

S'tya-Yg'Nalle (The Whiteness) is a fictional entity created by James Ambuehl and E. P. Berglund for their 1997 short story "Whiteout".

S'tya-Yg'Nalle, also known as "The Whiteness", is an ally or avatar of Ithaqua, stated to be one of the most powerful servitors of the Great Old Ones. Manifesting as what appear to be "snowflakes", they are actually tiny white crawling forms with pincer claws, similar to crabs or spiders. Despite their snowflake-like appearance, the particles actually generate extreme heat.

The Whiteness is said to be a portion of Ithaqua, much like how the Blackness is a portion of Nyarlathotep. Such as with Yin and Yang, the Whiteness and the Blackness are not considered opposites and cannot be used against each other, as they are aspects of space and time as one, consorting as "brothers". The Blackness moves through the stream of time while the Whiteness fills the spaces.

The Whiteness can be summoned using the Nyarlathotep ritual of Ob-ran, the Dark Herald of the Angled Howler, if the name of Ob-ran is interjected with "S'tya-Yg'Nalle". Targeted by the summoner, the rival caster will become a gateway for the Whiteness to enter this dimension, devouring the fabric of the rival caster's flesh from the inside. However, it can also be turned against the summoner, if the rival caster shouts out the Vach-Viraj incantation, a protection spell against the Great Old Ones, while dousing the summoner in the Tikkoun Elixir, also known as holy water, leading to the summoner being devoured instead. Once the feeding is over, the Whiteness will melt away into the body, disappearing as the lifeless shell is reduced to a torn and ragged state. (: "Whiteout")
